payload.title: Aleph integrity verification is disabled by default, allowing tampered vendored Aleph payloads to pass CI
payload.description: The new gate skips the Aleph bundle integrity workflow whenever the base branch has `.loa.config.yaml` set to `aleph.enabled: false`, which this diff also makes the repository default. Because the Aleph files remain vendored in-tree, a PR can modify `.claude/aleph/**`, `.claude/skills/loa-aleph`, `.loa-aleph.lock.json`, or `tools/aleph-release-ingest.py` while the dedicated integrity workflow no-ops and the Aleph unit suites skip. That creates a supply-chain integrity bypass: malicious Aleph code can be merged without the bundle verification that previously protected consumers who later opt in or invoke the vendored command paths.
payload.impact: An attacker with PR merge path can land modified vendored Aleph artifacts without required integrity checks, creating delayed code execution risk for users or CI jobs that later enable or run Aleph.
payload.recommendation: Keep the runtime/install/sync behavior opt-in, but do not skip integrity checks for diffs touching Aleph-controlled paths. For PRs, run the integrity workflow when Aleph paths or lock files changed, regardless of the base config gate, or add a separate required job that fails on Aleph path changes unless the integrity verification runs successfully.
